principles.text: Reuse code you already shipped and launch an MVP in about a week; paying customers are the real validation.
Sell a lifetime deal for early cash and validation, then move the product to subscription pricing.
If you dislike marketing, build growth into the product: a branded badge on free output, share links and embeds.
Build what customers ask for, but hold one-off requests until several customers want the same thing.
Spread risk across several businesses like a stock portfolio; buying a validated product can beat starting from zero.

sampleQA.question: How should I validate and launch a new SaaS product?

answer.text: Reuse code you already shipped: he built Testimonial's MVP in about a week and launched on Product Hunt the next day.
Skip long validation. People paying you is the ultimate validation, not replies saying it looks cool.
Open with a lifetime deal: $199 lifetime access sold 30 deals ($6K) in two weeks; PDF.ai's $99 deal got 300+ adopters.
Then switch to subscription pricing once demand is proven.

sampleQA.question: How do I grow without a marketing team?

answer.text: Lean on product-led growth: the Testimonial logo on free widgets brings signups and pushes users to upgrade to remove it.
Customers sending collection links and embedding walls creates backlinks and traffic.
After every feature: help article, email campaign, Twitter and LinkedIn post, blog post. There is no shortcut.
A 30% recurring affiliate commission brings 10-15% of revenue, and an exact-match domain like pdf.ai drives search traffic.

sampleQA.question: When should I quit my job to go full time?

answer.text: Quit after revenue validation, not before. He set a public goal to quit at $1K MRR.
Agree the downside with your family: he promised his wife he'd return to a job if he missed $100K ARR in a year.
Find out what actually blocks you. If it's money, take funding; if it's product-market fit, validate first.
Unpaid leave is a middle path that creates urgency while limiting risk.
